candidates.teaser: What if aging was optional? One creature on Earth might have figured it out...
candidates.video_title: Lobsters Don't Actually Age — Here's Why
candidates.video_description: Lobsters produce an enzyme that repairs their DNA indefinitely, making them biologically immortal. They don't weaken with age — they actually get stronger. Find out what eventually kills them.
candidates.script: What if you never had to age? Lobsters might have cracked that code. Unlike most animals, lobsters produce an enzyme called telomerase that continuously repairs their DNA. This means they don't weaken, slow down, or deteriorate with age. In fact, older lobsters are often more fertile than younger ones. A lobster doesn't die of old age — it usually dies from exhaustion during molting, disease, or being caught. Some scientists believe lobsters could theoretically live forever under perfect conditions. So the real question is — if you could stop aging, would you want to live forever?

candidates.topic: The Eiffel Tower has a secret apartment
candidates.teaser: There's a private room hidden at the top of the Eiffel Tower — and almost no one has ever been inside.
candidates.video_title: The Secret Apartment Inside the Eiffel Tower
candidates.video_description: Gustave Eiffel built a private apartment at the very top of the Eiffel Tower and refused all offers to rent it out. He used it to entertain some of the greatest minds of his era. The room still exists today.
candidates.script: Most people look up at the Eiffel Tower without knowing there's a secret apartment hidden at the very top. Gustave Eiffel, the man who built it, constructed a private living space for himself — complete with a piano, wooden furniture, and a laboratory. Wealthy Parisians reportedly offered enormous sums to rent it for just one night, but Eiffel refused every single offer. He used the apartment to host guests like Thomas Edison. The room still exists today, preserved almost exactly as Eiffel left it. And here's the twist — you can actually see it, but you can never stay the night. Would you visit?

candidates.topic: Humans have a fourth type of vision receptor
candidates.teaser: You might be seeing colors right now that don't officially exist — and science can prove it.
candidates.video_title: Some People Can See Colors That Don't Exist
candidates.video_description: A rare genetic mutation gives some people a fourth type of cone cell in their eyes, allowing them to distinguish up to 100 million colors. Most humans only see around one million. These people are called tetrachromats.
candidates.script: Most humans see around one million colors, and we think that's impressive. But some people are born with a genetic mutation that adds a fourth type of cone cell to their eyes — and those people can see up to one hundred million colors. They're called tetrachromats, and most of them are women. The extra cone sits between red and green, detecting shades the rest of us literally cannot process. What's wild is that many tetrachromats don't even know they have this ability — they assume everyone sees what they see. So what if the world you're seeing right now is actually a blurry, color-blind version of reality?

candidates.topic: The moon is drifting away from Earth
candidates.teaser: Every single year, the Moon quietly moves a little further away — and the consequences are massive.
candidates.video_title: The Moon Is Slowly Escaping Earth's Gravity
candidates.video_description: The Moon drifts about 3.8 centimeters away from Earth every year due to tidal forces. Billions of years ago, it was dramatically closer — and Earth's days were only six hours long. Eventually, the Moon may leave us entirely.
candidates.script: Every year, the Moon moves about three point eight centimeters further away from Earth — and it's been doing this for billions of years. When the Moon first formed, it was roughly fifteen times closer than it is today. Back then, Earth's days lasted only about six hours because the Moon's gravity was spinning our planet much faster. As the Moon drifts further, our days slowly get longer. Scientists calculate that in the far future, the Moon may drift so far that total solar eclipses become impossible — the Moon will simply be too small to cover the Sun. Makes you wonder — are we living in Earth's golden era right now?

candidates.teaser: Your old brick phone was actually more dangerous than your modern smartphone — and the reason is counterintuitive.
candidates.video_title: Old Nokia Phones Were More Harmful Than iPhones
candidates.video_description: Older mobile phones like the Nokia 3310 emitted significantly higher levels of radiation than modern smartphones. Better network coverage means today's phones work harder with less power. The phone you think is safer might actually be the riskier one.
candidates.script: You probably think your old Nokia brick phone was safer than today's smartphones. It turns out the opposite is true. The Nokia 3310 had a radiation output nearly three times higher than most modern iPhones. Here's why — older phones had to work much harder to grab a weak 2G signal, blasting out more radio frequency energy in the process. Modern smartphones operate on dense, powerful networks, so they need far less power to stay connected. The phone that survived being thrown across the room was quietly the more intense emitter all along. So which phone do you think was sitting in your pocket the longest?
